title: Romeo & Juliet
subtitle: Some love stories are meant to be lived.
author: After William Shakespeare

beats.title: A voice in the dark
beats.text:
I hear him before I see him.

Below my window, the orchard holds its breath.

What light is that above me? She does not know I am here, and still she lights the whole of this dark garden.

Then my name rises out of the dark, spoken by the boy whose hand found mine only hours ago.

Juliet.

Romeo. Here. With every reason to stay away.

beats.title: He is waiting
beats.text:
If anyone finds him here, his name alone will condemn him. I should send him away.

The walls are high and the penalty is death, if any of her kinsmen find me. I climbed them anyway.

He does not know I am listening. He speaks as though the night itself might answer him.

Instead of drawing the curtain, I move closer to the window.

choices.title: Lean into the moonlight
choices.flavor:
I lean beyond the stone sill. “Romeo.”

You know my voice, and I have hardly spoken. Call me love, and I will answer to nothing else.

His face lifts toward mine, and the courage I borrowed from the darkness becomes my own.

For one small moment, I forget to be afraid.

choices.title: Stay hidden. Listen.
choices.flavor:
I stay behind the curtain a moment longer.

She speaks and says nothing. Two of the fairest stars in heaven could not do the work her eyes are doing.

Let the night keep me, then. I will not go home to a house that has no word of her in it.

Then I step into the moonlight. “Romeo.” I have heard enough to know I want him to stay.

beats.title: More than a name
beats.text:
Montague. A word I was taught to hate before I knew the person it belonged to.

It is only a word. It is not my hand, nor my face, nor any part of me you have looked at.

But a name has never held my hand. A name has never looked at me as if the whole crowded room had fallen silent.

Then bid me be called something else, and I will be it before you have finished asking.

If I could set our names down here, between us, what would be left except him and me?

Only this. Only us, and the little distance of a wall.

I spoke first tonight. I do not regret a single word of it.

I heard what he said of me when he thought no one was listening. No name could say it better.

beats.title: Let it be true
beats.text:
By the moon I swear — by that blessed moon, that tips the tops of these trees with silver —

I stop him. The moon changes; I cannot bear the thought of this changing with it.

Then by what shall I swear?

By nothing. Or by yourself, if you must swear at all.

Then by myself. And if I am ever less than I am tonight, let my own name shame me.

Nothing grand, I think. Only come back tomorrow. Only mean it when daylight finds us.

beats.title: A promise, softly
beats.text:
My heart is yours. It has not been my own since I saw you across that crowded hall.

The words hang between the window and the earth, too large for the little distance they have to cross.

I should weigh them. I should ask how many girls in Verona have heard him speak this well.

I have never wanted to believe anything so much.

choices.flavor:
“And mine is yours.” I say it before fear can make the words smaller.

Then I am the happiest man ever to stand in a garden he had no right to enter.

If his purpose is marriage, I will send someone tomorrow to learn the time and the place.

Send them early. I will have been at Friar Laurence’s door before the bells.

I mean it. Ask the Friar at dawn, if you doubt me. I will already be waiting there.

I let myself believe him. Tomorrow, I will send someone to learn the time and the place.

My yes is quiet. It is still a yes.

beats.title: Until tomorrow
beats.text:
We say good night as though saying it slowly might keep the morning away.

Good night. Good night. I could say it a hundred times and still be standing here.

Go. The light is coming, and it does not love us.

Then I will go, and be nothing all day, and come back at dark and be a man again.

At last he goes. I stay at the window, holding the silence he has left me.

Tomorrow, I think. Such a little word to carry so much happiness.

I heard you. Say it again tomorrow, and I will come.

Then go, before I call you back a second time.

Until dark, then. I will count every hour of the day.

beats.title: A fragile plan
beats.text:
Friar Laurence has married us in secret. For a little while, I have been Romeo’s wife.

I gave him my heart before fear could make the words smaller. Fear has found other words since.

I asked him whether it was true. The Friar’s blessing made it so.

Then Tybalt is dead by Romeo’s hand, Romeo is banished, and my father has promised me to Paris.

A wife of one night, and already another man’s name is being set beside mine.

I come back to the Friar with no safe place left to put my hope.

beats.title: Forty-two hours
beats.text:
The Friar places a small vial in my hand. A sleep so deep that everyone will believe I am dead.

Forty-two hours, he says. Then I will wake.

He will send a letter to Romeo in Mantua, and Romeo will know the truth of it.

He will come to the tomb and be beside me when I open my eyes.

He turned back once when I called his name. He will turn back again.

I let him go that morning without calling after him. Now I must let a letter go the same way.

beats.title: For the life beyond this
beats.text:
Alone in my chamber, I lift the vial. What if I wake too soon? What if no one comes?

There is no one left to ask. The Nurse would tell my mother, and my mother would tell my father.

I picture Romeo’s face beneath my window.

I have already promised him tomorrow.

choices.flavor:
I steady my hand. “Romeo, I come.”

I drink, and set the empty vial down. I cannot make the world kinder by wishing it so.

But I can reach for the life we were promised.

I lie down with his name still warm in my mouth.

choices.flavor:
My hand will not stop trembling. I let it tremble. “Romeo, I come.”

I drink. The cup is lighter than the fear, and empties sooner.

Courage, perhaps, can be this small: a frightened girl choosing the only door she can see.

I lie down and imagine his hand finding mine in the dark.

beats.title: Carry my hope to him
beats.text:
The room grows distant. The candle softens into a single wandering star.

Somewhere beyond these walls, a letter will be making its way toward him.

My hand was steady when I drank. Let the letter travel as steadily.

My hand trembled, and I drank anyway. Let that be enough.

Carry it quickly. Put it in his hands before he hears anything else.

I hold that thought until I cannot hold anything at all.

beats.title: The world without your voice
beats.text:
Here is my love, and here I will stay. Eyes, look your last. Arms, take your last embrace.

I wake to stone beneath my hands.

The Friar is here. Romeo is here, too, but he does not turn when I say his name.

There is an empty cup beside him. I touch his cheek. It is colder than the orchard ever was.

Whatever he said in this room, he said it to a girl he believed was already gone.

I was here. I was here the whole time, and I could not answer him.

In the orchard I answered him before he had finished speaking. Here, I could not answer at all.

In the orchard I listened while he did not know. Here, I could not even listen.

beats.title: Too late
beats.text:
The Friar tells me his letter never reached Mantua. He urges me to leave; the watch is coming.

But Romeo came here believing I was gone. He was not wrong for a single hour, and it cost him everything.

All our tomorrows have narrowed to this silence.

I told him I was coming. I did not know he would be the one to go ahead.

I was afraid of waking alone. I never imagined waking to this.

I stay beside my husband when the Friar flees.

beats.title: One more moment
beats.text:
I kiss him. His lips are still warm.

Only a little time has come between us. Less than a morning.

Less than all the good nights we could not bear to finish.

That morning I called him back from the wall. I call him now, and he does not turn.

That morning I let him go without a word. I will not let him go so quietly again.

I press my forehead to his and whisper his name once more.

beats.title: What if…
beats.location: Between what was and what might have been
beats.text:
What if the letter had found me?

She thanked me for the orchard. Let me give her more than a wall to climb.

She asked me to wait for her. Let me imagine a world where neither of us had to wait.

Just once, let me imagine a world that gave us enough time.

beats.text:
I am already on the road when the messenger calls my name.

I break the seal with shaking hands. Laurence’s writing.

Juliet lives. Her stillness is a borrowed sleep, and I must be there when it ends.

I read those words again. Juliet lives.

beats.title: Every mile, your name
beats.location: The road to Verona · An imagined ending
beats.text:
I ride with the letter against my heart.

The road is the same road. Verona still holds the same dangers.

But every mile carries me toward her now, instead of toward a world without her.

Wait for me, Juliet. Only a little longer.

beats.title: This time, I am here
beats.location: The Capulet tomb · An imagined ending
beats.text:
In the tomb, I kneel beside her and take her hand.

I wait through the stillness, through every frightened breath.

I rode through the dark to be here. Now I must learn to be still.

I came slowly and surely. I can wait a little longer.

Then her fingers move against mine. Her eyes open.

Romeo?

Yes. I am here. I have not been anywhere else.

She gave me her heart without asking for proof. Here is the proof. I came.

She once asked me whether I was certain. I am certain now, kneeling here.

Then the daylight has not undone us after all.

beats.title: The beginning we never had
beats.text:
I have no promise that the world outside will forgive us.

Only her hand in mine, and the Friar waiting to lead us out.

Take me out of this place. Whatever we owe Verona, we will pay it in daylight.

I would carry her to the gate if she asked it.

Only walk beside me. That is all I ask.

I would climb every wall in Verona again for this.

No one waits for anyone now. We go out together.

For the first time, I am not too late.

I rode hard enough to outrun the old ending.

I came steadily, and I came whole, and I am still in time.

For now, that is enough to begin.
